clues: He was born in Makkah.
He was an orphan, raised by his grandfather and then his uncle.
He received revelation in the cave of Hira.
He migrated to Madinah.
The Qur'an calls him the Seal of the Prophets.
easy.explain: Muhammad ﷺ is the final messenger. Surah Al-Ahzab calls him the Seal of the Prophets, and Surah Al-Fath names him directly.

clues: He was a prophet, and the Qur'an mentions him many times.
He lived in the time of Ibrahim and believed in him.
His people committed an evil no nation had done before them.
Angels visited him as guests.
His wife was among those destroyed with his people.
easy.explain: Lut warned his people against their indecency. The angels told him to leave at night with his family, except his wife, who stayed behind with the people.

clues: He was a prophet and the grandson of Ibrahim.
He is also known as Isra'il.
He had twelve sons.
He wept until his eyes turned white with grief.
He was the father of Yusuf.
easy.explain: Ya'qub, son of Ishaq, grieved for years over Yusuf. The Qur'an tells how his sight returned when Yusuf's shirt was cast over his face.

clues: He was a prophet.
His birth was announced to his parents by angels.
His mother laughed at the news because she was old.
His son became a prophet too.
He was the son of Ibrahim and Sarah.
easy.explain: The angels who visited Ibrahim brought the news of Ishaq, and after him Ya'qub. The Qur'an praises Ishaq among the righteous prophets.

clues: She was a respected merchant of Makkah.
She hired a young man of Quraysh to trade for her.
She later married him.
She comforted him after the first revelation and took him to Waraqah.
She was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
easy.explain: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was the Prophet's first wife and the first to believe in his message. After the first revelation he returned to her, and she reassured him.

clues: She was the daughter of a close companion.
She narrated a great many hadith.
Verses in Surah An-Nur declared her innocent of a slander.
The Prophet ﷺ passed away in her room.
She was the daughter of Abu Bakr.
easy.explain: Aishah bint Abi Bakr was one of the Prophet's wives and among the most knowledgeable companions. The verses of Surah An-Nur were revealed about the slander against her.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's four daughters.
Her mother was Khadijah.
She married Ali ibn Abi Talib.
She was the mother of Hasan and Husayn.
The Prophet ﷺ said she was a part of him.
easy.explain: Fatimah was a daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah. He said, "Fatimah is a part of me."

clues: He was a merchant of Makkah and a close friend of the Prophet ﷺ.
He was among the very first to accept Islam.
He freed many enslaved Muslims, including Bilal.
He hid with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave during the Hijrah.
He became the first caliph.
easy.explain: Abu Bakr was the Prophet's companion in the cave, which the Qur'an refers to as "the second of two". He led the Muslims as the first caliph.

clues: He was known for his strength and strict sense of justice.
At first he was hostile to Islam.
His acceptance of Islam strengthened the Muslims in Makkah.
He began dating years from the Hijrah.
He was the second caliph.
easy.explain: Umar ibn al-Khattab became the second caliph after Abu Bakr. Ibn Mas'ud said the Muslims became powerful from the day Umar embraced Islam.

clues: He was a wealthy merchant known for his modesty.
He married two of the Prophet's daughters.
He was known by the title "possessor of two lights".
He sent standard copies of the Qur'an to the main cities.
He was the third caliph.
easy.explain: Uthman ibn Affan married Ruqayyah and later Umm Kulthum, daughters of the Prophet ﷺ. As the third caliph he had the Qur'an copied and the copies sent to the provinces.

clues: He was raised in the household of the Prophet ﷺ.
He was among the first to accept Islam, while still a boy.
He married Fatimah.
The Prophet ﷺ said he was to him as Harun was to Musa.
He was the fourth caliph.
easy.explain: Ali ibn Abi Talib was the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law. The Prophet ﷺ told him, "You are to me like Harun was to Musa."

clues: He was enslaved in Makkah.
He was tortured on the hot sand for his faith.
Abu Bakr bought his freedom.
He was known for his beautiful voice.
He was the first muezzin of Islam.
easy.explain: Bilal ibn Rabah endured torture saying "Ahad, Ahad" (One, One). Umar said of Abu Bakr that he was our master and freed our master, meaning Bilal.

clues: He was a strong warrior and a skilled hunter.
He was one of the Prophet's uncles.
His acceptance of Islam made the Quraysh think twice.
He was killed at Uhud.
He is called the master of the martyrs.
easy.explain: Hamzah, the Prophet's uncle, was martyred at the Battle of Uhud. Wahshi, who killed him, later accepted Islam and told the story himself.

clues: He was a gifted military commander.
He fought against the Muslims at Uhud.
He accepted Islam a few months before the conquest of Makkah.
He took the banner at Mu'tah after three commanders fell.
The Prophet ﷺ called him the Sword of Allah.
easy.explain: At Mu'tah, after Zayd, Ja'far and Ibn Rawahah were martyred, the banner went to "a sword from the swords of Allah", Khalid ibn al-Walid.

clues: He came from the tribe of Daws in Yemen.
He came to Madinah around the time of Khaybar.
He stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ to learn from him.
He narrated more hadith than any other companion.
His nickname means "father of the kitten".
easy.explain: Abu Hurayrah narrated more hadith than any other companion. He explained that while others were busy with trade and farms, he stayed with the Prophet ﷺ.

clues: He was one of the Prophet's uncles.
He opposed the Prophet ﷺ openly.
His wife was also hostile to the message.
A whole surah condemns him and his wife.
His name appears in Surah Al-Masad.
easy.explain: Abu Lahab is the only opponent of the Prophet ﷺ named in the Qur'an. Surah Al-Masad was revealed about him and his wife.

clues: He ruled Egypt.
He claimed to be a lord.
He ordered the killing of the sons of Bani Isra'il.
He drowned while chasing Musa and his people.
The Qur'an says his body was preserved as a sign.
easy.explain: Fir'awn (Pharaoh) claimed, "I am your lord, the most high." He drowned in the sea, and the Qur'an says his body would be preserved as a sign for those after him.

clues: She lived in Egypt.
She took baby Musa into her home.
Her husband was a tyrant.
She prayed for a home with Allah in the Garden.
She was the wife of Fir'awn.
easy.explain: The Qur'an gives the wife of Fir'awn as an example for the believers. The Prophet ﷺ named Asiyah among the women who reached perfection.

clues: He is an angel.
He is named in the Qur'an.
He is named in Surah Al-Baqarah together with Jibril.
The Qur'an warns that enmity to him is enmity to Allah.
His name is often written Michael in English.
easy.explain: Mika'il is one of the two angels named in Surah Al-Baqarah, alongside Jibril. The Prophet ﷺ also mentioned him in his night prayer supplication.

clues: It is a mosque.
It is the largest mosque in the world.
Prayer in it is worth more than prayer anywhere else.
Muslims everywhere face it in prayer.
The Ka'bah stands in its centre.
easy.explain: Masjid al-Haram in Makkah surrounds the Ka'bah. The Qur'an commands the believers to turn their faces towards it in prayer.

clues: It is a valley near Makkah.
Pilgrims stay there during Hajj.
It is known as a city of tents.
The pillars of the Jamarat are there.
Pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq there.
easy.explain: Mina lies between Makkah and Muzdalifah. Pilgrims go there on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and return after Arafah to stone the Jamarat.

clues: It lies on the route of the Hajj.
Pilgrims arrive there after sunset on the day of Arafah.
They pray Maghrib and Isha there together.
Many pick up their pebbles for stoning there.
The Qur'an calls a place there the Sacred Monument.
easy.explain: Pilgrims leave Arafah after sunset and spend the night at Muzdalifah. The Qur'an tells them to remember Allah at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram).

clues: They are two small hills.
They are now inside the Masjid al-Haram.
Hajar ran between them looking for water.
Pilgrims walk between them seven times.
The Qur'an calls them among the signs of Allah.
easy.explain: Sa'i is the walk between Safa and Marwah. The Qur'an says they are among the symbols of Allah.

clues: It is a small cave on a mountain near Makkah.
The Prophet ﷺ used to go there to worship alone.
He would take food with him for several nights.
Jibril came to him there.
The first verses of the Qur'an were revealed there.
easy.explain: Before prophethood, the Prophet ﷺ would retreat to the cave of Hira. There Jibril came with the first verses: "Read in the name of your Lord."

clues: It is on a mountain south of Makkah.
Two men hid there for three nights.
The Quraysh searched for them right up to its mouth.
One of the men said, "Do not grieve, Allah is with us."
The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid there during the Hijrah.
easy.explain: During the Hijrah the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in the cave of Thawr. The Qur'an recalls the moment he said, "Grieve not, Allah is with us."

clues: It is a mountain.
It lies just north of Madinah.
A major battle was fought at its foot.
Hamzah is buried near it.
The Prophet ﷺ said it loves us and we love it.
easy.explain: Mount Uhud overlooks Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ said, "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."

clues: It is a cemetery.
It is in Madinah, next to Masjid an-Nabawi.
Many companions are buried there.
The Prophet ﷺ would go out at night to pray for those buried there.
Its full name is Baqi' al-Gharqad.
easy.explain: Al-Baqi' is the main cemetery of Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ visited it and prayed for its people.

clues: It is a land across the Red Sea from Arabia.
Its king was known for his justice.
Muslims fled there to escape persecution in Makkah.
Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke before its king.
Its king was the Negus, al-Najashi.
easy.explain: Muslims migrated to Abyssinia twice during the Makkan period. When the Negus died, the Prophet ﷺ led the funeral prayer for him in his absence.

clues: It is a prayer.
It is prayed after Isha.
It is prayed in an odd number of rak'ahs.
Many make it the last prayer of the night.
Its name means "odd".
easy.explain: Witr is prayed after Isha and before Fajr in an odd number of rak'ahs. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Make witr the last of your prayers at night."

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It is prayed in daytime.
Its time begins after the sun has risen well above the horizon.
Abu Hurayrah said the Prophet ﷺ advised him to pray two rak'ahs of it.
It is named after the forenoon.
easy.explain: Abu Hurayrah said his friend ﷺ advised him to fast three days each month, pray two rak'ahs of Duha, and pray witr before sleeping.

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
It has no ruku' and no sujud.
It is prayed standing with four takbirs.
Attending it earns a reward like a mountain.
It is prayed for a Muslim who has died.
easy.explain: The funeral prayer is offered for the deceased. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever attends it until the prayer is offered gets one qirat of reward, and a qirat is like a mountain.

clues: It is a call.
It is said just before the obligatory prayer begins.
Its words are close to those of the adhan.
It includes the phrase "the prayer has begun".
Bilal was told to say its phrases once and the adhan's twice.
easy.explain: The iqamah is the second call, given when the prayer is about to start. Bilal was ordered to say the adhan phrases twice and the iqamah phrases once.

clues: It is recited in the prayer.
It is said while sitting.
It begins with greetings to Allah.
It includes the testimony of faith.
Ibn Mas'ud said the Prophet ﷺ taught it to him as he would teach a surah.
easy.explain: The tashahhud is recited in the sitting of the prayer. It begins "At-tahiyyatu lillah" and ends with the testimony of faith.

clues: It is needed for every act of worship.
It is in the heart, not on the tongue.
It turns a habit into worship.
The first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari is about it.
The word means "intention".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will have what they intended."

clues: It is made from the twig of a tree.
It is used every day.
It cleans the mouth.
The Prophet ﷺ would have ordered it before every prayer if it were not hard on people.
Its other name is siwak.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "If it were not hard on my followers, I would have ordered them to use the siwak before every prayer."

clues: It is a phrase repeated often.
It is said aloud by men.
It is said by people in ihram.
It is said until the stoning on the day of Eid.
It begins "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk".
easy.explain: Pilgrims in ihram repeat the talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am. You have no partner, here I am."

clues: It is an act of worship done once a year.
It involves an animal.
Its time begins after the Eid prayer.
The Prophet ﷺ offered two rams.
It is the sacrifice of Eid al-Adha.
easy.explain: Udhiyah is the sacrifice offered on Eid al-Adha and the days after it. Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed two rams.

clues: It is connected to a happy occasion.
It involves sacrificing an animal.
It is done for a child.
It is traditionally done on the seventh day.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "With the boy there is an aqiqah."
easy.explain: Aqiqah is the sacrifice for a newborn. The Prophet ﷺ said, "With the boy there is an aqiqah, so slaughter for him."

clues: It is a meal.
It is sunnah to hold one.
Guests who are invited should accept.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "even if only with one sheep".
It is the wedding feast.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ told Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf after his marriage, "Give a wedding banquet, even if only with one sheep."

clues: It is a kind of charity.
Its reward keeps coming.
It continues after a person dies.
Building a well or a mosque can be an example.
Its name means "flowing charity".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said that when a person dies their deeds end except for three: an ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for them.

clues: It is a day of the year.
Fasting it is sunnah.
It falls in Muharram.
Musa and his people were saved on it.
It is the 10th of Muharram.
easy.explain: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah he found the Jews fasting Ashura because Allah saved Musa on that day. He said, "We are closer to Musa than you," and fasted it.

clues: It is a month.
It is one of the four sacred months.
Ashura falls in it.
The Prophet ﷺ called it "the month of Allah".
It is the first month of the Islamic year.
easy.explain: Muharram opens the Hijri year. The Prophet ﷺ said the best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month of Muharram.

clues: It is a month.
It comes just before a very important month.
The Prophet ﷺ fasted more in it than in any month other than Ramadan.
It is the eighth month of the Islamic year.
Ramadan comes straight after it.
easy.explain: Aishah said she never saw the Prophet ﷺ fast a whole month except Ramadan, and never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.

clues: He is an angel.
Every living soul will meet him.
He has helpers among the angels.
He takes souls at the appointed time.
The Qur'an calls him the angel of death who is given charge of you.
easy.explain: Surah As-Sajdah says the angel of death, who has been given charge of you, will take your souls, then you will be returned to your Lord.

clues: They are two angels.
They come after burial.
They question a person in the grave.
They ask about his Lord, his religion and his prophet.
Their names are mentioned in a hadith in Jami' al-Tirmidhi.
easy.explain: A hadith in al-Tirmidhi (graded hasan) names the two angels of the grave as Munkar and Nakir.

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
Everyone will have to cross it.
Some cross it like lightning, others crawl.
It is set over Hell.
It is a bridge.
easy.explain: The Sirat is the bridge laid over Hell on the Day of Judgement, described in the long hadith of Abu Hurayrah in Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
Nothing will be wronged on it, even a mustard seed.
Good and bad deeds are placed on it.
Heavy good deeds mean success.
It is the scale.
easy.explain: Allah says He will set up just scales on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least, even if it is the weight of a mustard seed.

clues: It is a stage everyone will pass through.
It begins at death.
It lasts until the Resurrection.
Those in it cannot return to this world.
Its name means "barrier".
easy.explain: Surah Al-Mu'minun says that behind those who die is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised.

clues: They are a creation of Allah.
Most people cannot see them.
Some of them are believers and some are not.
They were created from smokeless fire.
A whole surah is named after them.
easy.explain: The jinn were created from smokeless fire. Surah Al-Jinn tells of a group of them who heard the Qur'an and believed.
